findings.summary: The proposed Advisor exception says a fallback consult found blocking gaps (e.g. missing contracts for K3-10..K3-15 and an inconsistent scope rule), and that the fix lives in findings-round-revision-2.md, to be committed after approval and 'binding wherever more precise'. That file is not one of the five digest-bound sources and was not supplied. The sources assert it is not a sixth authority (Spec §18 says additional files are not authority sources, and design.md names exactly five sources). Spec §21 and the traceability map cite register IDs only up to K8-4 and K3-9 and cite no K3-10+, K1-8, K4-7, K4-9, K2-6b, K8-5 or K5-7. Without the register, full coverage cannot be shown from the sources. Approving these bytes would bind the PO to text known to be incomplete, with the correction held outside the package. The consult itself has no receipt (consultation/report null), so its claims are unverified.

Spec §21.4 (R4) lets an agent self-dispatch the canonical role template when a native route fails, and the course accepts the result as that role's evidence with a fallback label. The listed roles include readiness. Spec §17 requires independent readiness to be backed by host-observed freshness, read-only effects and terminal state, and says a model-authored claim cannot satisfy this. PRD §14 also forbids weakening Critic/Advisor independence. R4 defines no mechanism to enforce freshness or read-only behaviour for a self-dispatch, or to bind its result to the dispatch (R4-2 only says a self-review is 'refused'). Whether fallback can ever satisfy readiness or the Advisor gate is unresolved, and the answer changes the authority predicate.

R1-4 (Spec §21.1) admits `node scratch/<script>.mjs` as read-only when argv has no write target and the script is 'not a known writer'. The epic's own measured finding (PRD §1.2, Spec §4.1/§4.2) is that staging a payload in a file and executing it defeats parameter-text classification. Spec §5.2 item 3 and PRD §7.3 require unresolved interpreter writes to stay fail-closed, and PRD S2 requires zero indirection routes. 'Known writer' is a denylist, and no mechanism is given for verifying a script's content or effects. The design either contradicts S2 and B2-iii or leaves the rule undefined, and it must state which. The negative test (a writer script writing outside scratch/) does not say how the writer is detected.

The headline requirement is that the PO is asked exactly twice (plan, push). Spec §21.3 also says every signature-mode push, including each feature-checkpoint push, needs an exact-commit signed approval, so more than one push means more than one approval. The same bullet allows remaining ceremonies if listed in an inventory with reasons, which contradicts 'exactly two'. Other sources add possible PO acts: per-key TOFU confirmation (Spec §5.2.4), explicit repository enrollment (PRD §12), and R3's 'key setup'. R3-1 asserts 'exactly two' proofs without defining the scenario (number of pushes, first-time key, enrollment). The acceptance test cannot be evaluated until 'exactly two' is defined.

Spec §21 and traceability disagree on row ownership. K4-3 is in R1's header but mapped to R3 (R3-4/R3-5). K7-3 is 'read part' under R2 but mapped to R1-1. K5-1 is mapped to R5-1 in traceability but absent from §21.5's list. K7-7 has no acceptance case (traceability gives only '§21.6'). K7-8 has no case and no reproduction-step owner. Traceability sends many unrelated rows (K3-5, K3-6, K5-5, K5-6, K7-7, K7-8) to one catch-all backlog item, and several mapped items predate 2026-10-03, so design-input's 'one backlog item per finding cluster' is not demonstrated. The '40 findings' in design.md cannot be reconciled with the roughly 48 IDs cited. The register and the backlog items were not supplied.

R1-2 requires a greenfield draft course to reach `present-plan` with zero guard overrides. Reaching present-plan depends on later-sequenced work: R4 role routes (Advisor/readiness on Claude/Windows and Antigravity), R5 authoring sequence and Verify-contract precondition (R5-4 refuses presentation without it), and R3 signing. Spec §21.7 and design.md put R1/R2 first and R5/R3 later, so R1's own acceptance case cannot be met by R1 alone. Per-slice acceptance versus end-to-end acceptance should be separated.

PRD §7.12/§14 and Spec §21.7 make the three-runner happy-path scenario the completion test. Cases R1-1..R6-4 are unit- or fixture-level, and no end-to-end case with a defined host/OS matrix is enumerated (Claude Windows and POSIX, Codex incl. WSL, Antigravity). Traceability refers to AC-26..AC-31 in acceptance.md, which was not supplied, and AC-32 appears only in the exception text. Per-runner host evidence is required but the scenario steps are not itemised.

The formal Advisor route ended `unavailable` (no child started, no input submitted). Consultation, report, receipt and disposition are null. The proposed exception cites a fallback consult and a PO chat decision to 'approve revision 1 with binding obligations'. None of this is receipt-backed in the supplied evidence. The claim that the revision route is Codex-only and that revision is impossible before approval is not stated in any of the five sources (Spec §17 describes an ordered revision chain). A claimed prior PO chat approval conflicts with the 'one final PO decision' framing and cannot count as readiness. The exception stays non-authorizing and must be judged by the PO.

Spec §20 and PRD §13 define a proposed attended external recovery CLI and legacy-custody archival, but give no owning work package, backlog item, wave placement or acceptance-case IDs. PRD §7.11 lists recovery in the epic acceptance list while saying it is 'design input only', so completion criteria are ambiguous. The trust bootstrap for the pinned CLI and the public signer anchor 'outside the broken runner' is only described as operator-selected. The user's 'Es muss immer eine Möglichkeit geben' is met only as typed-unavailable plus a handoff for several cases, and design-input labels this a bounded interpretation. The requirement to fix the actual current stuck state ('mach das heile') is deferred to P1 source confirmation with no schedule.

R4 makes the Claude dispatch guard accept built-in types (Explore, Plan, general-purpose) and run Advisor-prohibition parsing only when the line is present. The PRD §14 non-goals keep template-only briefings and Advisor/Critic independence. The sources do not say whether built-in types remain template-bound, budget-counted and write-scoped, and R4-4 tests only that Explore is admitted. A negative case is missing.

R2 admits exact-file reads on `\\wsl.localhost\...` and `\\wsl$\...` paths, and says credential roots stay denied 'through every spelling'. The WSL-side credential roots (for example distro-home .ssh/.gnupg) and how they are enumerated are not defined. R2-2 tests only one UNC credential path. This is a security surface that needs an explicit enumeration and negative cases.

The PRD `technical-spec-sha256` marker equals the supplied Spec digest (9137adbe…958c). The five source paths and digests in the envelope match the bundle and the Advisor initial-context sources. design-input, design and traceability consistently state that no approval, receipt, host evidence or implementation authority is claimed. The preserved German recovery requirement is quoted verbatim and the 2026-10-03 PO requirements are carried into PRD §14 and Spec §21.

structured_output.summary: Not ready for PO review. The five sources are internally consistent on bindings: the PRD's spec digest matches the Spec, and the digests match the envelope. The original recovery requirement and the 2026-10-03 PO requirements are carried through. But the Advisor route ended unavailable. The only substantive review is a fallback consult with no receipt in the bundle, and it reports blocking and major gaps. The package was not revised. The proposed exception defers the corrections to a post-approval document that is outside the digest-bound sources. Independently of that, four design problems remain. R4 lets self-dispatch cover readiness, which conflicts with the Spec §17 host-observed independence requirement. R1-4's scratch-script admission conflicts with the epic's own payload-indirection finding and S2. 'Exactly two PO approvals' is contradicted by signed checkpoint pushes and by allowed residual ceremonies. Register coverage cannot be shown complete, and Spec §21 and traceability disagree on several row mappings. Non-blocking gaps: R1-2 acceptance depends on later slices, there is no end-to-end three-runner case or host matrix, the recovery route has no owner, sequencing or completion status, and the WSL credential-root and built-in-agent-type rules are under-specified. This is a readiness assessment only, not approval, and it grants no exception or implementation authority.
